title: Objective Measurement of Nocturnal Erections Following Radical Prostatectomy to Guide Early Erectile Function Rehabilitation Using the 2N8 Measurement System (2N8 Study)
summary: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is the most common functional side effect following radical prostatectomy (RPX) and significantly impacts patients’ quality of life. Guidelines recommend early, multimodal erectile rehabilitation; however, objective assessment of progress is limited in everyday clinical practice. Currently, evaluation is based primarily on patient-reported outcomes (PROMs), such as the IIEF-5 and EPIC-26. However, these are subjective and may lead to a delay in intensifying treatment. This study investigates whether an objective home monitoring system for measuring nocturnal erections (2N8) enables a more precise assessment of progress and can serve as the basis for standardized, data-driven intensification of therapy.

interventions.name:
Conducting nocturnal erection measurements using the 2N8 system, for 4 nights at each measurement time point. 4 measurement time points: preoperative, early postoperative, 3 months post-op, and 12 months.
Additional data collection via PROMs (IIEF-5, EPIC-26)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy
Preoperative erectile function: IEEF >19
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing severe erectile dysfunction
Absolute and relative medical contraindications for SKAT therapy (e.g., anticoagulation, increased risk of priapism in multiple myeloma, induratio penis plastica, thrombocytopenia)
